title: A heavier planet of equal radius
hook: Change planet mass and predict surface gravitational acceleration.
misconception: surface gravitational acceleration stays fixed when planet mass doubles.
objective: Apply g = GM/R² to compare surface gravitational acceleration when planet mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a spherically symmetric planet with fixed radius, g = GM/R². When planet mass doubles, surface gravitational acceleration becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model g = GM/R²; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a spherically symmetric planet with fixed radius, with a nonzero initial result. If planet mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on surface gravitational acceleration?
recall.why: Apply g = GM/R² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
